title: The Last Lonely Integer
statement: A positive integer $n$ is called lonely if there is exactly one ordered pair of positive integers $(a,b)$ with $a \le b$ and $5a+13b=n$. Find the largest lonely integer.
hints: Suppose $(a,b)$ satisfies $5a+13b=n$. Look for a way to change $a$ and $b$ so that the value of $5a+13b$ stays the same.

Use the general solution of a linear Diophantine equation. Since $\gcd(5,13)=1$, every integer solution of $5x+13y=n$ has the form $(a+13t,\,b-5t)$ for an integer $t$. Work out when the steps $t=1$ and $t=-1$ give another valid pair.

The step $(a-13,\,b+5)$ fails only if $a\le 13$, and the step $(a+13,\,b-5)$ fails only if $b\le a+17$. So a lonely integer must meet both conditions. Maximise $5a+13b$ under them, then check that the maximising pair really is the only pair for its value of $n$.
solution: Let $n$ be lonely, with unique pair $(a,b)$, where $1\le a\le b$ and $5a+13b=n$. Replacing $(a,b)$ by $(a+13t,\,b-5t)$ for any integer $t$ does not change $5a+13b$, since the change is $65t-65t=0$. If $a\ge 14$, then $(a-13,\,b+5)$ is a second valid pair, because $1\le a-13\le b+5$. So $a\le 13$. If $b\ge a+18$, then $(a+13,\,b-5)$ is a second valid pair, because $a+13\le b-5$ and $a+13$ is positive. So $b\le a+17$. Therefore $$n=5a+13b\le 5a+13(a+17)=18a+221\le 18\cdot 13+221=455.$$ It remains to show that $455$ is lonely. The pair $(13,30)$ is valid, since $13\le 30$ and $5\cdot 13+13\cdot 30=65+390=455$. Because $\gcd(5,13)=1$, any integer solution $(x,y)$ of $5x+13y=455$ has $x-13$ divisible by $13$, which gives $(x,y)=(13+13t,\,30-5t)$ for some integer $t$. If $t\le -1$, then $x\le 0$, which is not allowed. If $t\ge 1$, then $x\ge 26$ and $y\le 25$, so $x>y$, which is not allowed. Only $t=0$ remains, so the pair is unique. The largest lonely integer is $455$. Why this works. linear-diophantine-solving, bounding: all solutions differ by multiples of $(13,-5)$, so uniqueness forces upper bounds on $a$ and $b-a$ that together bound $n$.
